verdict: The revision closes the direct forgery and race holes the first round found (A5, S2-under-lock, src_* coverage, stage keyed by submitter, S1 uniform Denied, FreezeGroup, expect_genesis), but several of the new rules collide with each other or with the guarantees they were added to protect. Substantiated: S9 applies to the authority and refuses the second RemoveIdentity carry on a shared group within 30 s, so 'always wins' is broken again by the fix that was meant to protect kicks; A5 makes the specified backup-key replacement (G4/R6 force a rotate, author is the retiring backup key, which is no longer pinned) unverifiable everywhere; the re-genesis defence is only as strong as an ambiguous P2 sentence and a chart entry per group that no API helps the operator fill; StageVersions widened to any registered identity re-opens the group-existence oracle S1 was carefully closed against and adds a per-identity disk budget of 2x every group; G6 as worded restricts every addition to one id per record (times S9's 30 s) while still admitting the one-id stale resubmission it was written for; the rotating half of the two-step revocation is not durable across a restart, leaving a group write-fenced with the removed key holding the live M. Remaining items are liveness and wording gaps around FreezeGroup, the rogue-admin escalation ladder, the two-key window, and the operator's pin reset.

unfixed_prior.prior_title: RemoveIdentity in mode A ... breaking the 'always wins' guarantee (authz-B) / Authority carry removing a reader with no fence (authz-A)
unfixed_prior.why_not_fixed: D13's two-step (carry under the lock, rotate outside, Put fence) restores 'always wins' only if the carry is always accepted. 6.3 says every server-authored record goes through the same verifier, and S9 ('at most one accepted non-rotating record per author per group per 30 s') lists no exemption for author == authority. Two RemoveIdentity calls, or a legacy Grant shrink followed by a RemoveIdentity, on identities sharing a group within 30 s: the second authority carry is refused 'S9: rate'. Separately the rotating half is an in-process retry loop with no startup resumption, so a crash between carry and rotate leaves the group fenced with the removed key still holding the live M (see findings 1 and 6).
unfixed_prior.fix: Exempt author == authority and kind == recovery from S9 (its target is admin churn). Add a startup and post-install sweep of secret_group.needs_rotation = 1 that re-launches the authority rotate.

unfixed_prior.prior_title: Re-genesis under a known name is accepted by every replica that has no pin (authz-A)
unfixed_prior.why_not_fixed: P2 now rejects an unconfigured genesis unless --tofu, but the sentence 'a genesis whose keys or hash differ from the configuration is rejected ... Without configuration and without a pin ... TOFU only when --tofu' leaves open whether expect_keys alone (the chart values that exist today) counts as configuration. The attacker holds the operational key, so keys match; if matching keys suffice, the original attack is intact for every name without an expect_genesis entry. Nothing returns the genesis hash the operator must put in bunker.expectGenesis (Status carries head_hash only), and every new group is unmirrorable until the chart is edited, which pushes deployments to --tofu (see finding 3).
unfixed_prior.fix: State that for a name with neither pin nor expect_genesis entry the genesis is rejected regardless of expect_keys unless --tofu; add genesis_hash to Status and to `client epoch status`; consider a per-name tofu list.

unfixed_prior.prior_title: SubmitEpoch's recovery exception turns its error replies into a group-existence oracle (authz-A)
unfixed_prior.why_not_fixed: Fixed for SubmitEpoch (S1 uniform Denied, C3-under-head.backup first), but the same fix round opened StageVersions to 'any registered identity' with reply Ok. The server must resolve group -> group_id to key the stage and apply the per-(group, submitter) cap, so an unknown group cannot answer Ok without saying so; any distinct answer is the oracle docs/protocol.md section 6 forbids ('nonexistent group ... indistinguishable'). See finding 4.
unfixed_prior.fix: Gate StageVersions like S1 (uniform Denied unless the caller holds a bit on the group or presents a recovery record verifying under head.backup), or specify 'Ok and discard' for unknown groups and bound staged bytes per submitter bunker-wide.

unfixed_prior.prior_title: An online kick target starves the client-signed kick (authz-B) / kick target stalls kicks and recoveries (authz-A)
unfixed_prior.why_not_fixed: S9 limits non-rotating records only; a target that is an admin can author rotates without limit (cheap on a small group) and, more simply, one carry that clears the kicker's admin bit (G5 lets admins edit a/w bits of others via carry) makes the kicker fail A2 on rebase and Denied on the 'guaranteed fallback' legacy Grant (authorize_group PERM_ADMIN, server.rs:676); once the rogue is the last admin, admin_count <= 1 (server.rs:709-716) refuses every legacy shrink of it. The only path left is RemoveIdentity or recovery, which the spec has, but 6.1 step 8 and 7.4 ('undone by a surviving admin') misstate the ladder. See finding 7.
unfixed_prior.fix: Replace 'guaranteed fallback' with the explicit ladder: client kick -> legacy shrink (requires requester still admin, target not last admin) -> RemoveIdentity (service admin, always wins) -> recovery.

findings.section: 5 S9 vs 6.3 (server-side revocation), D13, 7.4 'Compromised reader key'
findings.title: S9 rate limit applies to the authority and refuses the second RemoveIdentity carry on a shared group within 30 s
findings.detail: S9: 'at most one accepted non-rotating record per author per group per 30 s'. 6.3: 'All server-authored records go through the same verifier'. RemoveIdentity authors an authority carry per affected group 'under the lock, in one transaction' and is 'Never blocked'. Sequence, mode A, prod = {alice: rwa, bob: r, carol: r}, both bob's and carol's laptops stolen: t0 RemoveIdentity(bob) -> carry #n+1 on prod by authority, accepted, needs_rotation = 1, server rotate starts. t0+5s RemoveIdentity(carol) -> carry #n+2 on prod by authority -> S9 'rate' (rotate #n+2 by the server may or may not have landed; if it has, the carry is still the second non-rotating authority record inside 30 s). Either the whole RemoveIdentity answers Failed{'S9: rate'} (compromised key stays registered and readable) or the identity row is deleted with the carry skipped (carol stays in the head ACL with a valid wrap, replicas keep serving her until an unsigned `revoked` entry arrives, and the server's rotate re-wraps M_new to her because A3's acl subset of head.acl includes her). Same for legacy Grant shrink then RemoveIdentity, and for RemoveIdentity's w-only carries. The rule that was added to protect kicks against churn breaks the one revocation the design calls unconditional.
findings.fix: S9 applies to non-authority, non-recovery authors only (its purpose is admin churn). State it in S9 and in 6.3, and add the test 'two RemoveIdentity within 30 s on identities sharing a group: both carries land'.

findings.section: 5 A5 vs A4, G4, R6, 6.4 'Backup replacement', 4.1 pinned()
findings.title: A5 makes a backup-key replacement unverifiable: the retiring backup key authors a rotate it is no longer a recipient of
findings.detail: 6.4: 'Backup replacement (--backup <id>, a rotate too) needs only the meta update'. G4: a recovery that replaces backup 'MUST be a rotate (R6)'. A5: 'rotate, and recovery with a new generation: author in recipients(rec)'. A4: recovery author == head.backup (the OLD key). pinned(rec) = {rec.backup (NEW)} u {authority}; readers(rec) is the acl. The old backup id is in recipients(rec) only if the operator lists it in --acl as a reader, which keeps the retired (possibly compromised) root as a reader of the new M and is exactly what the rotate exists to prevent. So every verifier (server, replica, client, auditor) refuses the specified backup-replacement recovery with 'A5'. Section 13 tests A5 ('refuses a self-kicking rotate') and 'recovery replacing authority with the server running on two keys' but never a recovery replacing backup, so the contradiction ships. Authority replacement is unaffected (backup stays pinned); A->E mode change is unaffected.
findings.fix: Scope A5 to kind = rotate, or add the handover case explicitly: for kind = recovery, A5 is satisfied when author == head.backup and either author in recipients(rec) or rec.backup != head.backup. Add the negative/positive test pair (backup replacement lands; a recovery whose author is neither pinned nor a reader and whose backup is unchanged is refused).

findings.section: 10 P2, P4, C1, 11 (client pin file), 9 Status, 17 criterion 4
findings.title: The re-genesis defence hinges on an ambiguous P2 sentence, an operator-filled hash no API returns, and a TOFU client pin file
findings.detail: (1) P2: 'a genesis whose keys or hash differ from the configuration is rejected (unpinned-genesis). Without configuration and without a pin, genesis is trust-on-first-use only when --tofu is set'. A replica configured with expect_keys only (bunker.expectAuthorityId/expectBackupId, no expectGenesis entry for 'prod') is 'configured'; the compromised node holds operational.key, so its genesis' for 'prod' (fresh group_uid, acl {K_att: rwa}, wraps to {K_att, authority, backup}, prod's ciphertext re-encrypted under M') has keys that equal the configuration and no hash to differ from. Under the natural reading it is accepted without --tofu; the prior finding's sequence then runs unchanged for every unpinned name. (2) Even under the strict reading, every CreateGroup afterwards needs a chart change with the new group's genesis hash before the operator can mirror it; Status returns head_hash and group_uid but not genesis_hash, and `client epoch status` is not specified to print it, so operators will run --tofu, which is the attack window per new name. (3) The client pin file (11) is 'TOFU on first sight' with no expect-genesis flag: an admin's first `client grant`/`kick` against a compromised node verifies and signs onto whatever chain the node serves, and the admin's signature on the fake roster is then presentable to --tofu replicas and auditors.
findings.fix: P2: 'for a name with no pin: accept the genesis iff expect_genesis[name] == hash; if there is no expect_genesis entry, reject unless --tofu, regardless of expect_keys'. Add genesis_hash to Status and print it in `client epoch status`/`log` and in CreateGroup's CLI output so the chart entry is copy-paste. Give the CLI `client epoch pin --group g --genesis <hash>` and make first sight print the genesis hash and require confirmation unless --tofu.

findings.title: StageVersions open to any registered identity is a group-existence oracle and a per-identity disk budget of 2x every group
findings.detail: The fix for the recovery-staging gate made StageVersions 'any registered identity (n/a)' with reply Ok and a cap of 2 x total retained ciphertext + 16 MiB per (group, submitter), 15 min idle TTL, 6 h ceiling. (a) The handler must resolve `group` to key epoch_stage(group_id, submitter, stage_id) and to compute the cap; for an unknown group it cannot store anything and cannot compute a cap, so it answers something other than Ok (Failed, or Denied while a known group gets Ok). protocol.md section 6 makes 'nonexistent group ... indistinguishable' a protocol invariant and S1 was rewritten specifically so SubmitEpoch 'must not be a group-existence oracle'; StageVersions now is one for every registered identity, including write-only CI keys. (b) Any registered identity may hold Sum over groups of (2 x retained + 16 MiB) on disk, renewing the idle TTL with one small StageVersions per 15 min for 6 h, then a new stage_id. With 100 groups of 10 MiB retained that is ~3.6 GiB per identity, from an identity with no bit on any of them.
findings.fix: Gate StageVersions like S1: uniform Denied unless the caller holds any bit on the group, or the first StageVersions of the stage carries `recovery: bstr` whose C3 verifies under head.backup (evaluated before any other reply). If 'any registered identity' is kept, specify 'unknown group: answer Ok, store nothing' and add a bunker-wide per-submitter budget (e.g. 2 x the largest group's retained bytes + 16 MiB) with an audited 'stage-cap' rejection.

findings.title: G6 as worded restricts every grant to one id per record and still admits the stale-ACL revival it was written against; rotates are not covered at all
findings.detail: G6: 'A later rewrap MAY re-add an id absent from head.acl only if the record's ACL delta relative to head consists solely of that addition'. Every id being added is by definition absent from head.acl, and a verifier comparing acl to head.acl cannot tell 're-add' from 'add'. Literal effect: a rewrap that adds two readers, or adds one reader and changes anyone's w/a bit, is refused by every verifier; with S9 (one accepted non-rotating record per author per group per 30 s) onboarding ten readers is ten records over five minutes and the TUI's multi-toggle flows break. Meanwhile the backstop misses its target: head h = {alice: rwa, bob: rwa, dave: r}; alice computes a repair rewrap (unchanged ACL, allowed by S6) against h; bob's rotate h+1 kicks dave; alice's submit -> EpochConflict; a client that resubmits the computed ACL (the 6.2 rule forbids it, but G6 exists precisely for the non-compliant case) has delta {+dave} relative to h+1, which G6 accepts as a sole-purpose re-add: dave is back with the live M, attributed to alice. And G6 names only rewrap: a rotate is free to carry any ACL (nothing in R/A/G bounds a non-authority rotate's ACL growth), so a stale rotate resubmitted after a legacy shrink of bob (bob still registered, S2 passes) revives bob with M_new and clears needs_rotation.
findings.fix: Define 'revived id' as an id present in the ACL of a record in a bounded lookback (e.g. the last 8 records, or since its last appearance) but absent from head.acl; G6 constrains only records that add a revived id (sole addition, any kind), never first-time adds. Or drop the server backstop and keep the 6.2 client delta rule plus the EpochConflict diff. Either way state that rotates are bound by the same rule as rewraps.

findings.section: 6.3 'The rotating half', D13, 8 needs_rotation, 12 step 3 (serve), 5 S10
findings.title: The two-step revocation's rotate is an in-process retry with no restart resumption; a crash leaves the group write-fenced with the removed key holding the live M
findings.detail: 6.3: the authority rotate is performed 'immediately after, outside the lock ... retried with backoff until it lands; the flag clears on its commit'. needs_rotation is a durable column, but nothing in 6.3, 12 step 3 or serveloop says a starting server scans secret_group.needs_rotation = 1 and re-launches the rotate (the only startup derivation mentioned is the R5 seen-sets). Sequence: RemoveIdentity(bob) at t0 (carry lands, flag set, Put fenced); the process is restarted at t0+2s (deploy, OOM, relay self-heal restart per serveloop). From then: every Put on prod answers Failed{'needs-rotation'} indefinitely, bob's stashed DEK still opens the live generation of the authoritative file and every replica mirror, and the only exit is an admin noticing '!' and running `client rotate`. Q8 sells the window as 'seconds'. Two related gaps: the retry must observe the flag under the lock and stop when an admin's rotate cleared it (unstated), and it is unstated whether S10 refuses the authority rotate as a 'non-recovery SubmitEpoch' — if it does, a RemoveIdentity during a freeze leaves the flag set until the recovery lands, and that recovery, authored offline against the frozen head, now fails C2 because the carry moved the head.
findings.fix: Add to 6.3 and 12: at serve startup and after every install transaction the server enqueues an authority rotate for each group with needs_rotation = 1 (audited 'rotate-resume'); the retry re-reads the flag under the lock and exits when clear. State that S10 does not apply to authority-authored records (they are shrink-only and clear the fence sooner) and that 6.4 step 1 exports only when Status shows frozen && !needs_rotation.

findings.section: 6.1 step 8, 6.3 legacy Grant, 7.4 'Compromised admin key', G5, S9
findings.title: One carry by the target defeats both the client-side kick and its 'guaranteed fallback'; 7.4's 'undone by a surviving admin' is false after it
findings.detail: head h = {alice: rwa, bob: rwa, carol: rwa}. bob (compromised) authors carry h+1 with acl = {alice: rw, bob: rwa, carol: rw}: G5/A2 allow an admin to edit others' a/w bits with recipients unchanged, S6 is satisfied, S9 permits it (one record), cost one round trip. alice's rotate against h -> EpochConflict; rebase -> A2 fails (alice not admin in h+1). alice's legacy Grant{bob, 0} -> authorize_group(PERM_ADMIN) -> Denied (server.rs:676-678). carol likewise. A service admin's legacy Grant{bob, 0} -> admin_count(prod) == 1 -> Failed 'cannot remove the last admin' (server.rs:709-716, which 6.3 keeps). Only RemoveIdentity(bob) (orphans prod) plus a backup recovery re-adding alice/carol, or FreezeGroup + recovery, remains. 6.1 step 8 calls legacy Grant 'the guaranteed fallback' and 7.4 says a rogue admin is 'undone by a surviving admin'; neither survives this sequence, and an operator following 6.1 will discover the ladder during the incident.
findings.fix: State the escalation ladder explicitly in 6.1 step 8 and 7.4: client kick -> legacy shrink (requester must still be admin in the projection; target must not be the last admin) -> RemoveIdentity (service admin; orphans; always wins) -> recovery. Consider letting a service admin's legacy shrink bypass the last-admin guard when the group is frozen, so the rogue can be removed without deregistering its key.

findings.title: FreezeGroup does not stop Delete or Get, so the rogue admin it 'holds off' can destroy every secret between freeze and export and reads throughout the ceremony
findings.detail: S10 refuses non-recovery SubmitEpoch, legacy Grant and Put. Delete is write-gated (server.rs:448) and `DELETE FROM secret` cascades every secret_version (store.rs:1331, schema ON DELETE CASCADE): a rogue admin holds w (G1 forces r on admins; w is what admins have in practice) and can delete every name of the frozen group before the operator's export in step 1, so the recovery bundle re-encrypts nothing and the group is restored only from a snapshot. Get is unaffected, so during the hours-long offline ceremony the rogue keeps reading, on the authoritative node and on every replica. The spec's own stronger tool, RemoveIdentity(rogue), denies immediately, drops the row on every replica at the next sync and rotates in seconds; 6.4 step 0 recommends the weaker one first.
findings.fix: S10: a frozen group refuses every mutation (Put, Delete, legacy Grant, non-recovery SubmitEpoch). 6.4 step 0: 'RemoveIdentity the rogue if its key can be deregistered (immediate denial, automatic rotate); freeze when it cannot or when several admin keys are suspect'.

findings.title: Two-key window: S2 says install adopts the record's authority/backup into meta, 6.4 says meta advances only when no head names the old key; CreateGroup mints new groups under the retiring key meanwhile
findings.detail: S2: 'the install adopts the record's authority/backup/mode into meta'. 6.4: 'when none does [name the old authority], meta.operational_ed25519 is advanced (audited authority-rotated)'. If S2 wins, meta flips on the first recovery and CreateGroup's genesis ('authority ... equal the server's configured values') uses the new key from then on, but a later recovery for another group that keeps the old backup (no --backup) writes the old backup back into meta.backup_ed25519, so groups created after it are rooted on a key the operator has retired. If 6.4 wins, every CreateGroup during the (possibly long) window mints genesis with the compromised operational key as authority and recipient, and each such group needs its own recovery. S7 ('ids equal to a configured authority/backup are refused') also reads differently under the two.
findings.fix: meta.operational_ed25519/backup_ed25519 are advanced only by an explicit operator step (`db set-authority --next` when GroupStatus shows no group naming the old key; `db set-backup`), never by an install; during the window CreateGroup uses the configured next operational key and the configured backup; S2 for recovery compares against {current, next} for authority and does not touch meta.

findings.title: The freeze is not stated to be checked in the install transaction, and 'export after freeze so prev is stable' is false against RemoveIdentity
findings.detail: S8 verifies outside the lock; S3 CAS and install are under it. A rogue's record verified before FreezeGroup landed installs afterwards unless the frozen flag is re-read inside the install transaction; the spec states the freeze only as a request-level answer. The recovery is then authored against a head the rogue moved once more (one extra ceremony round, not a starvation). Independently, RemoveIdentity is (correctly) not frozen, so any removal touching the group between step 1's export and step 3's submit moves the head and the recovery fails C2; 6.4 does not warn the operator.
findings.fix: S10: the frozen flag is evaluated under the lock together with S3; 6.4 step 1: 'export only when Status reports frozen and needs_rotation = false; a RemoveIdentity touching the group during the ceremony invalidates the bundle (re-export, re-sign)'.

findings.title: A busy or hostile writer starves a client-side rotate in mode A; FreezeGroup cannot help because it blocks the admin's own SubmitEpoch
findings.detail: S4: stragglers up to 16 MiB per commit are re-encrypted by the server; beyond that the reply is StaleVersions and the client stages exactly those. A write-only identity issuing MAX_VALUE-sized Puts (about 4 MiB each) produces more than 16 MiB of stragglers in the seconds a client needs to restage and resubmit, so every SubmitEpoch of an explicit `client rotate` answers StaleVersions again. The server-side revocation is immune (Put fence) but exists only for a kick target; an explicit rotate or a kick whose target the admin does not want deregistered has no fence. Mode E specifies 'a write fence while a stage from an admin is open'; mode A does not. FreezeGroup refuses every non-recovery SubmitEpoch, so freezing the writer freezes the rotation too.
findings.fix: In mode A, while a stage from an admin of the group is open (within idle TTL), Put on the group answers Failed{'rotation-pending'} (the mode-E fence, already specified); or account straggler bytes per writer and refuse the writer's Put, not the rotation, above the bound.

findings.section: 10 P4, 'The k8s operator', D9, 6.4 last paragraph
findings.title: The operator has no specified pin-reset path after an authoritative restore, and chart expect values vs. the pins Secret have no precedence rule
findings.detail: P4 names `db reset-pin` (mirror file) and `Replica::reset_group(group, expected_genesis)` (library). The operator's pins live in `<release>-bunker-pins`, written on every accepted head and loaded at boot, and the chart's expect* values 'seed the first boot'. After an authoritative restore (D9: replicas 'are reset by the operator') the Secret holds the newer head, every boot reloads it, the restored chain is a rewind, and BunkerSecrets stay Ready=False/ChainRejected until someone edits or deletes the Secret by hand, which the spec never says and which bypasses the 'pin-reset' audit. If the operator instead updates bunker.expectGenesis, nothing says whether a chart value overrides a stored pin (if it does, the pin protection of P1 is bypassed by any chart edit; if it does not, the update is a no-op).
findings.fix: Specify: the stored pin wins over chart values; a one-shot chart value `bunker.resetPins: {prod: <genesis_hash>}` (or an annotation on the BunkerSecret) makes the operator call reset_group, rewrite the Secret row and audit 'pin-reset'; document the manual Secret edit as the break-glass path.
